statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 7% (low) with Nasdaq-100 futures inside the CME weekend halt and no live price path available.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold because no tradable price path can form while index futures are halted through 22:00 UTC on Sunday. Stress is elevated on 2007-high Treasury yields and on the reported rejection of Iran's seven-day Hormuz plan, which leaves an unpriced geopolitical variable to be absorbed at the reopen.
headline: Weekend halt with Hormuz diplomacy rejected: Tail low, Stress elevated on 2007-high yields
body: Nasdaq-100 index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, eleven hours beyond the end of this forecast window, so every hour assessed here sits inside a closed market. Friday's cash session ended constructively and without pathological structure: NDX closed 30,608.14, up 0.42%, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and below its 30,770.63 52-week high, while the S&P 500 added 0.51% to 7,743.41 and the Dow 0.93% to 51,828.62. VIX fell 5.1% to 14.87, near the low of its 14.68-15.94 range. Delayed latest-session megacap data was dispersed rather than one-way, with MSFT up 3.7% and QCOM up 4.0% against META down 3.3% and INTC down 3.5%; that reads as rotation, not the persistent directional efficiency Tail measures. Meta's roughly 13% weekly gain on its Muse AI agent was the week's largest single-name contribution. The material change since the previous assessment is geopolitical rather than technical: Reuters, citing the Wall Street Journal, reports that Washington has rejected Iran's seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, with renewed strikes expected only after the November congressional elections. That removes the diplomatic relief which had pushed WTI down 7.4% on the week to $92.41, and leaves an unpriced variable to be absorbed at the Sunday reopen. Because the reported timeline is post-midterm rather than imminent, this raises Stress and weekend gap risk rather than establishing a near-term pathological price path. The durable stress source remains rates: H.15 puts the 10-year at 5.18% and the 30-year at 5.47% for Sep 24, the 10-year at its highest since 2007 and the long bond since 2004, driven by hawkish Barr remarks, firm energy and a hot PMI. Tail is therefore held at 7% across the window: a pathological price path cannot form in a closed market, and no observed shallow pullback, failed retracement or session-extreme holding exists to support a higher reading. Stress is elevated at 48% and drifts to 51% as unpriced weekend news accumulates toward the reopen. Mapped policy state: EA_ON.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the past twenty-four hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment; the 2026-09-25T13:00Z hour has none and remains explicitly unavailable. The window spans the back half of Friday's U.S. session, where Tail sat between 18 and 21 with WATCH mapped early and EA_ON from 15:00Z, and the post-settlement weekend halt, where Tail decayed to 7 and Stress eased from the mid-50s to the mid-40s as the session's directional question closed out.
outlookSummary: All twenty-four forecast hours fall inside the CME weekend halt, which runs until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, eleven hours past the end of this window. Tail is held in the 6-9 band throughout because a pathological price path cannot form in a closed market; the small late-window rise is accumulated gap risk ahead of the reopen rather than observed structure. Stress is elevated at 47-51 on 2007-high Treasury yields and on the reported rejection of Iran's seven-day Hormuz plan, which leaves the week's oil relief unwound and unpriced. The mode turns mixed in the final six hours to reflect genuinely two-sided rate, equity and geopolitical signals. Confidence decays from 82 to 76 as Friday's settlement ages with no live price path to refresh it.

Rates are the durable stress source, with the 30-year at its highest since 2004 and the 10-year at 5.18% on Sep 24; none of that resolves before Monday, and none of it can form a path during the halt.
